structured_output.world_model:
W3 (cost lens), after E015. The tip is E015: E010's recipe (Muon with 3 NS steps, Lookahead/EMA, resizing 24/28/32 at 40/30/30%, batch size 2000, last group 512, LS 0.3, 9.5 epochs, 238 steps) with the train step compiled in max-autotune, CUDA graphs on, and Muon compiled with reduce-overhead. It runs in 6.578 s at 0.7574.

CUDA graphs saved only 0.06 s (about 1%). That makes host/launch overhead under the 4-CPU pin small, about 1-3%, so GPU compute dominates. Accuracy moved +0.27 pp with "identical math". That is a kernel/RNG reshuffle, not a real gain. It shows recipe-level reshuffles of about ±0.3 pp are real, and that the tip's 0.44 pp margin is partly luck.

Budget: time ≈ F + V × pixel fraction, with F about 0.5-0.8 s (data upload, whitening, augmentation, interpolation) and V about 7.3 s at full resolution. A step takes about 25 ms of GPU compute. Systems levers are now nearly exhausted. Graph-break removal or folding augmentation into the compiled region is capped at about 0.1-0.25 s. The remaining large levers are FLOPs (epochs, pixels, width) and the fixed cost F.

Measured prices:
- compile: -14% time (E004).
- Lookahead/EMA: about +1 pp at 0 time (E005).
- Muon: +0.66 pp for +4% time (E006).
- Resizing 24/28/32: -22% time for about 0 to -0.6 pp (E007), a good trade.
- Aggressive resizing with 20 px and a 20% tail at 32 px: 0.9 s/pp, a bad trade (E011).
- Epochs: about 2 s/pp (E008).
- Width 576→512: about 1.6 s/pp (E010).
- CUDA graphs: -1% time (E015).

Hyperparameter nudges are all in noise: LS 0.2 gave +0.04 pp, Muon lr ×1.5 gave +0.10 pp, LR decay to 0 gave -0.07 pp. Muon renormalizes filter norms every step and applies no weight decay to filters. Weight decay only reaches the BN biases, whitening bias and head, so changing it should be near-noise.

Lookahead's fast-weight reset is probably part of its value. A plain EMA with a cubic alpha ramp has an end-horizon of about 20 steps and does little earlier, so I expect it to come in 0.2-0.6 pp worse.

Noise: per-seed std is 0.2-0.35 pp, so the 3-seed SE is about 0.15-0.2 pp. Compiled runs are bit-reproducible (E012). Time noise is about 1%.

With 0.44 pp of margin, the obvious exploit is spending it on epochs: 9.5→9.25 or 9.0 saves about 2.5-5% for about 0.1-0.25 pp. That is risky against the 40-seed judgment because part of the margin is reshuffle luck.

Misses: I underestimated known-good airbench components early on. Recent forecasts have been calibrated.

Unsure:
- The 40-seed offset (E012's held-out seed results are still not visible).
- The breakdown of F: how much of the time is spent in prepare, augmentation and interpolation, versus the steps.
- Whether a plain EMA would lose much against Lookahead.

forecasts.reason: Muon renormalizes the filters and they get no weight decay, so halving it only touches the BN, whitening-bias and head groups. Expect a reshuffle of about ±0.3 pp, not the +0.3 pp the hypothesis needs, at zero time cost.

CUDA graphs already removed most launch overhead (E015 saved only 1%). Augmentation and LR-tensor folding is worth at most about 0.1-0.25 s, under 3%, and a change to the RNG stream would make accuracy not bit-identical.
A plain EMA with a cubic ramp has a short end-horizon (about 20 steps) and loses Lookahead's fast-weight reset. Expect about 0.4 pp below the tip, with no time saving.

cruxes: What did E012's held-out seeds 3-12 show? Is the tip's 0.44 pp margin real, or reshuffle luck from the CUDA-graph change? This decides whether 9.5→9.25 or 9.0 epochs (-2.5 to -5% time) is safe.

How does the fixed cost F (about 0.5-0.8 s) break down across H2D upload, whitening eigh, per-epoch augmentation and antialiased interpolation, versus the per-step compute? Only F has systems slack left.
Does any accuracy-per-FLOP lever (BN-stat recompute, a longer 32 px tail with a shorter 24 px head) buy at least 0.3 pp cheaply enough to fund a further epoch or width cut?
